elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with nose symptoms and:
elements.text: Give urgent attention to the patient with nose symptoms and: Head injury with clear watery discharge from nose 30.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with nose symptoms and:

elements.text: 1History of anaphylaxis, urticaria or angioedema. 2Common triggers include pollens, household pets, house dust mite, cockroaches and moulds. 3If on lopinavir/ritonavir or atazanavir/ritonavir, avoid fluticasone. Discuss/refer instead.

• Advise on cough/sneeze hygiene and to wash hands regularly. While unwell, avoid contact with elderly/those with long-term health conditions. • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. • Explain antibiotics are not needed. • Advise to rest and keep hydrated. • Advise to return if worsening symptoms: if cough/difficulty breathing 23, if face pain 49, if ear pain 50.
Pain when pushing on forehead/ cheeks, headache worse on bending

Sinusitis likely • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. • Give sodium chloride 0.9% nose drops as needed. • Give oxymetazoline 0.05% 2 drops in each nostril 8 hourly as needed, maximum 5 days. Advise against overuse which may worsen blocked nose. • If symptoms ≥ 10 days, temperature ≥ 38°C, purulent discharge, face pain ≥ 3 days, or symptoms worsen after initial improvement, give amoxicillin 500mg 8 hourly for 5 days. If severe penicillin allergy1, give instead azithromycin 500mg daily for 3 days. • If recurrent, test for HIV 124. • If poor response to antibiotic, refer. • Refer same day if: - Tooth infection - Swelling over sinus or around eye - Neck stiffness.
Blocked/runny nose Ask about duration and associated symptoms:
most days for > 4 weeks. May have itchy eyes,

Allergic rhinitis likely • Help to identify and advise to avoid triggers2. • Give fluticasone3 nasal spray 100mcg (1 spray) in each nostril twice a day. Advise patient to aim nozzle outwards and upwards and avoid sniffing vigorously. • Give chlorphenamine 4mg 6-8 hourly as needed for up to 5 days only when symptoms worsen (side effect is sedation). • If nose very blocked at night, give oxymetazoline 0.05% 2 drops in each nostril at night for a maximum of 5 days. Advise against overuse which may worsen blocked nose. • If recurrent eye problem, check for allergic conjunctivitis 48. • If recurrent skin problem, check for urticaria and eczema 82. • If recurrent cough or wheeze, check for asthma 138. • Review after 3 months: if symptoms still not controlled despite good adherence to nasal spray, add cetirizine 10mg at night. • If symptoms severe and persist despite treatment, refer.
likely • Check throat: secretions or cobblestone appearance may be seen at back of throat. • Treat as for allergic rhinitis (see adjacent column). • If no improvement after 2 weeks, refer/discuss.
Sore throat or fever for less than 3 days
Any of: temperature ≥ 38°C, chills, nausea, sore muscles?
• Firmly pinch nostrils together for 10 minutes with patient sitting and leaning forward. • Check BP: - If SBP < 80, give sodium

chloride 0.9% 1L IV rapidly, repeat until systolic BP > 80. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens. - If ≥ 140/90 148. • If still bleeding, insert bismuth iodoform paraffin paste (BIPP) soaked ribbon gauze into nostril/s:
return next day to remove BIPP gauze. - If bleeding persists, refer

urgently. • If patient on aspirin or warfarin, doctor to review medication and if on warfarin, check INR. • Advise to avoid nose-picking and contact sport if recurrent bleeds. • If continually rubbing or itchy nose, consider allergic rhinitis (see adjacent). • If recurrent bleeds and no improvement with above management, refer.
Approach to the patient with nose symptoms not needing urgent attention If sore throat, mild fever and a thick grey layer in nose/throat (pseudomembrane), consider diphtheria 53.
